subject: Physics
description: Range, height, time of flight, parabolic trajectory, optimal angle

questions.stem: An object thrown into the air at an angle (in absence of air resistance) follows a path that is:

options.option_text: A straight line tilted at the launch angle
A parabola, due to constant downward gravity
A perfect circle around the centre of the earth
A spiral, due to the rotation of the earth

questions.explanation: Without air resistance, projectile horizontal velocity stays constant; vertical velocity changes uniformly with g. Resulting trajectory: PARABOLA. Galileo first showed this. Distractor 1 — straight line would need no gravity. Distractor 3 — circular orbit needs continuous central pull (orbital velocity). Distractor 4 — spirals would need rotational drag, irrelevant here.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: For a given initial speed, the angle that gives the MAXIMUM RANGE on level ground is:

options.option_text: 30° from the horizontal direction
45° from the horizontal direction
60° from the horizontal direction
90° from the horizontal direction

questions.explanation: Range R = u² sin(2θ) / g. Maximum when sin(2θ) = 1 → 2θ = 90° → θ = 45°. Range R_max = u²/g. Complementary angles (θ and 90°−θ) give the SAME range — e.g., 30° and 60°. Distractor 4 (90° = straight up) gives zero range.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: A ball is thrown horizontally from a tower. As it falls, the HORIZONTAL velocity component:

options.option_text: Decreases due to air resistance always
Stays constant in absence of air resistance
Increases as it falls under gravity force
Reverses direction at the highest point

questions.explanation: Gravity acts only VERTICALLY. So horizontal velocity component is unchanged in absence of air drag. Vertical velocity grows linearly downward. Two motions are independent → parabolic trajectory. Distractor 1 — true with air resistance, but ideal projectile assumption ignores it. Distractor 3 — gravity is vertical, so doesn't affect horizontal. Distractor 4 — direction doesn't reverse.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: At the highest point of a projectile's path, its VERTICAL velocity is:

options.option_text: Maximum at that highest point
Zero, just before reversing direction
Same as the initial vertical speed
Equal to the horizontal speed component

questions.explanation: Vertical velocity is u·sin θ at launch, decreases at rate g (deceleration on the way up), reaches ZERO at the apex (highest point), then accelerates downward. Horizontal velocity remains u·cos θ throughout. Distractor 1 — maximum at launch + landing, not at apex. Distractor 3 — same as launch only at landing. Distractor 4 — coincidence only if launch was at 45°.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: A projectile is launched at angle 30° with speed 20 m/s. Time of flight on level ground (g=10) is:

options.option_text: 1 second of flight time
2 seconds of flight time
3 seconds of flight time
4 seconds of flight time

questions.explanation: Time of flight T = 2u sin θ / g = 2 × 20 × sin 30° / 10 = 40 × 0.5 / 10 = 20/10 = 2 s. Distractor 1 — half. Distractor 3 — wrong sin. Distractor 4 — would correspond to a steeper angle.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: Two stones, one dropped from rest and another thrown horizontally, fall from the same height H. They:

options.option_text: Hit the ground at very different times
Hit the ground at exactly the same time
Have very different vertical accelerations
Reach the ground only along straight paths

questions.explanation: Vertical motion is independent of horizontal motion. Both stones experience the same gravity from the same height → same time to fall (T = √(2H/g)). The thrown stone covers more horizontal distance, but reaches ground at the SAME instant as the dropped one. Classic Galileo demonstration. Distractor 1 contradicts independence. Distractor 3 — both fall under same g. Distractor 4 — thrown stone follows a parabola.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The MAXIMUM HEIGHT reached by a projectile depends on which factor most directly?

options.option_text: The horizontal launch speed component
The vertical launch speed component
The total mass of the projectile body
The colour or shape of the projectile

questions.explanation: Maximum height H_max = u² sin² θ / (2g) = (vertical component)² / (2g). Depends on VERTICAL launch speed, NOT horizontal. Distractor 1 — horizontal component controls range, not height. Distractor 3 — mass irrelevant in vacuum (Galileo). Distractor 4 — shape matters only with air resistance.
